title: Typography — Justification, Optical Margins & Soft Hyphens

metadata.author: pdfnative-cli samples
metadata.subject: align justify, opticalMargins, soft hyphens (U+00AD), hyphenationLanguage (pdfnative 1.8.0)

blocks.text: Justified text with optical margin alignment

This paragraph is set with align: "justify". Every line except the last is stretched to the full measure by widening the inter-word spaces. With opticalMargins the punctuation that lands at a line edge — commas, periods, quotation marks and hyphens — hangs slightly into the margin, so the visual edge of the text block looks straight. "Quotation marks," for instance, and the trailing comma here, are pulled outward; a plain flush-left setting would leave a ragged optical edge. Justification works with the base-14 fonts and with any registered font; the narrow spaces and kerning of the other typography samples need a registered font.

A soft hyphen (U+00AD) marks a permitted break inside a word and is invisible unless the line breaks there: electro­magnetic, inter­national­isation, micro­processor, hyper­text, tele­communication, photo­synthesis, anti­disestablishment­arianism, counter­revolutionary, thermo­dynamics, extra­ordinary, multi­dimensional, inter­operability. The engine prefers a soft-hyphen break to an over-stretched line; the hyphen glyph appears only where the break happens. hyphenationLanguage is passed to a hyphenation provider when one is installed programmatically (setHyphenationProvider); the CLI ships none, so soft hyphens are the portable way to mark break points.
Left-aligned (the default): the right edge is ragged and the word spacing is even.
Centred: each line is centred on the measure.
Right-aligned: the left edge is ragged.
